title: SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department’s Beyond the Bell program is participating in the Summer Food Service Program this summer.  Free meals, which meet Summer Food Service Program federal guidelines, are available to all children 18 years of age and under and to persons over 18 years of age who are enrolled in a state approved educational program for the mentally or physically disabled.  The Food Distribution Program is available to all eligible participants without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex, or handicap.  Any person who believes that he or she has been discriminated against in any USDA-related activity should write immediately to the Secretary of Agriculture, Washington, DC 20250, or call toll free (866) 632-9992 (Voice).  Individuals who are hearing impaired or have speech disabilities may contact USDA through the Federal Relay Service at (800) 877-8339 or (800) 845-6136 (Spanish).  USDA is an equal opportunity provider and employer.

Free meals will be provided at the Beyond the Bell program from through August 13th.

Breakfast will be served at Beyond the Bell to program participants from 8:00 to 9:00 am and lunch will be served from 11:30 am to 12:00 pm.  Menus for both meals will be posted on Beyond the Bell’s Facebook page.

Clay County Health Department, the program sponsor, is located at 601 E. 12th Street in Flora.  For further information, contact Tamara Byers or Kathryn Holstlaw at 618-662-8322.

title: SMALL EQUIPMENT GRANT PROGRAM
full_story:
The Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM) announced the recipients of the 2026 Small Equipment Grant Program.  A total of $6 million was awarded to 260 fire departments/districts and EMS providers across the state.  The program was established to provide grants of up to $26,000 each for the purchase of small firefighting and ambulance equipment.

Local districts receiving grants include the Montrose Fire Protection District in Effingham County received $24,750, in Marion County the Kell Community Fire Protection District will get $26,000, and the Odin Fire District gets $18,500, in Wayne County the Bedford Township Fire Protection District will get $26,000, in Fayette County the St. Peter Fire Protection District gets $25,213 and in Jasper County the Wade Community Fire Protection District will get $17,089.

This program is an innovative approach to a problem that has long caused difficulties for fire departments and not-for profit ambulance services in Illinois, particularly those that have hardships in generating the necessary revenue for small equipment.  The purpose is to allow eligible applicants the opportunity to purchase small equipment that they may otherwise not be able to purchase.  The OSFM received 355 applications, requesting around $8.1 million in funding for this grant period.

Most Illinois fire departments, fire protections districts, township fire departments, and stand-alone, nonprofit ambulance service providers were eligible to apply.  All fire departments, fire protections districts and township fire department applicants were required to participate in the National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS) and National Emergency Response Information System (NERIS) for a minimum of two years prior to applying.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is asking you to donate blood as we head toward the summer months.  The organization says there is traditionally more of a need at this time of year and all blood types are needed, especially Type O, which can be used when a patient’s blood type is unknown.

There will be two Blood Drives next week.  The first is at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church on Tuesday, June 9th from Noon to 6 pm and the next is on Thursday, June 11th from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  Donors at these drives will receive a $15 gift card by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).

title: PLUMMER ICASH EVENTS
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer is hosting an ICASH event in partnership with the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office.  Constituents are encouraged to stop by to check if they are owed unclaimed property and receive assistance filing a claim.

State Senator Jason Plummer said, “Too often, folks don’t realize they may have money or property waiting to be claimed.  These ICASH events make it easy for residents to stop by, get help from professionals, and find out if they have unclaimed property.  My goal is to make this service more convenient and ensure people get the assistance they need to reclaim what’s rightfully theirs.  The Treasurer’s Office has over $5 billion in unclaimed property owed to Illinois residents.”

The ICASH event will be at the Flora Volunteer Fire Department on Tuesday, June 9th from 10 am to 2 pm.

ICASH events help residents across Illinois locate and reclaim unclaimed property.  Since 2015, more than $2.5 billion in assets have been returned to Illinoisans.  Unclaimed property can include everything from forgotten bank accounts and uncashed checks to insurance payments, stocks, and even the contents of safe deposit boxes.

No reservations are required.  For more information, call Senator Plummer’s office at 618-283-3000.

title: IGNITE CURIOSITY SUMMER CAMPS FCC
full_story:
Frontier Community College is inviting area students of all ages to explore new interests and develop hands-on skills through its upcoming Ignite Curiosity Summer Camps.  Registration is now underway for the camps which offer creativity and teamwork for a variety of age groups.

On June 11th at Frontier Community College in the MLT Lab will be Wrongfully Convicted, Forensic Science Camp.  In this interactive Camp participants will explore the world of DNA fingerprinting using professional miniPCR laboratory equipment.  The camp is for students in 7th through 12th grade and cost $45.  Drawing 1 on June 15th at 11 am where participants learn the basic techniques of drawing.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $35.  Whispering Colors on June 15th at 1 pm.  Students will experiment with watercolors.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $35.  Canvas 1 and 2 will be held on June 16th, with Canvas 1 starting at 8 and Canvas 2 starting at 12.  Canvas 1 is an introduction to acrylic painting and Canvas 2 builds on the skills learned in Canvas 1.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $35 for each class.  Lego Battle Bots will be held on June 16th at 8 am.  In this hands on robotics camp students will design, build, and program their own Lego battle bots while learning the basics of robotic coding.  The camp is for those in 3rd through 8th grade and cost $25.  Sign Language Camp will be held on June 17th starting at 1 pm.  Participants will be introduced to American Sign Language.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $25.

To learn more about these camps at FCC or about other camps at the other IECC campuses go to the iecc.edu/communityed website.  To sign up or register for the FCC camps, call or visit the Student Services Office at Frontier Community College.

title: FINNEY SENTENCED
full_story:
John W. Finney was sentenced to 75 years in prison Thursday in connection with the shooting death of his wife Amy on September 1st, 2025.  Finney was convicted of murder in late March after a four-day trial.

The Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office began work on this case when they received a report of a possible homicide in the county on September 1st.  Finney was pulled over in rural Du Quoin where according to the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office, they found Finney’s wife dead in the hatchback area of the vehicle.  Evidence revealed that the wife died from a gunshot wound during a domestic dispute at their home the day before.

title: EBIKE LAW
full_story:
Illinois has approved new regulations for electric bicycles, scooters and high-powered electric motorcycles that will take effect in the new year.  Senate Bill 3484 introduces several changes aimed at improving safety for pedestrians, cyclists and motorists.

Under the new law, all electric bikes and scooters will be prohibited from operating on sidewalks.  High-powered electric devices, often called “e-motos,” with motors exceeding 750 watts or capable of speeds greater than 28 mph will be classified as motor-driven cycles.  Riders of these vehicles will be required to have a driver’s license or permit, liability insurance and license plates.

The law also establishes age requirements for standard e-bike riders.

Individuals must be at least 15 years old to operate Class 1 and Class 2 e-bikes and at least 16 years old to ride a Class 3 e-bike.  Riders under the age of 18 will not be allowed to carry passengers unless they are immediate family members.

For e-scooters and hoverboards, riders must be at least 16 years old and may only operate them on roads with speed limits of 35 mph or less.

title: GAS TAX PAUSE
full_story:
Illinois lawmakers approved a measure to temporarily suspend the state’s scheduled motor fuel tax increase for six months, part of the broader $55.9 billion fiscal year 2027 budget passed by the General Assembly.

The move delays the annual automatic increase in the gas tax, which typically takes effect July 1st and is tied to inflation under a 2019 law.

Illinois’ gas tax is adjusted each year based on inflation to help fund road, bridge, and transit projects statewide.  The July 1st, increase was projected to raise the per-gallon tax slightly before lawmakers intervened.

By delaying the increase, state leaders say the measure is intended to provide short-term relief to drivers facing higher fuel prices and broader cost-of-living pressures.

Governor JB Pritzker previously indicated openness to pausing the increase, while also warning that doing so could reduce revenue used for transportation projects.

Supporters of the final budget say the pause is one of several steps designed to ease everyday costs, alongside measures like a back-to-school sales tax holiday.

The new fiscal year begins July 1st, when the increase would have otherwise taken effect.
